answer: An agent economy can make each account escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake and slash it when an adjudicated task shows coordinated duplicate identities claiming rewards. For example, agents may commit copper tokens before a jade-market prediction round; a public challenge reveals matching control or copied submissions, and losing accounts forfeit stake and access to future rounds. The ledge is that Sybils can still appear, but each additional identity now requires capital at risk, so cheap mass registration becomes costly and repeated attacks drain funds.
